newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on USDA production outlook.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on USDA production outlook.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a USDA Outlook Conference estimate for 1997 U.S. corn production at 9.63 billion bushels, above last year's output of 9.293 billion, traders said.
"The government numbers were a little bearish but it doesn't matter a lot because they haven't planted it yet and they won't for quite a while," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
USDA's Chief Economist Keith Collins told the Outlook Conference U.S. corn production could total "close to 9.6 billion bushels," the second highest ever.
He also said stocks could rise to more than 1.2 billion bushels.
The U.S. corn planting season begins in April and is usually at a rapid clip by late April and early May.

Corn was underpinned by USDA's weekly export inspections number. The government early Monday said U.S. corn inspected for export during the week ended February 20 totaled 41.497 million bushels, above trade expectations for 32 million to 35 million bushels.
Corn closed 1/2 to 3-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with March down 2-3/4 at $2.89.
But the corn market generally drifted Monday, with a late break in soybeans hitting prices and fund buying Monday sagged to about 15 million bushels.
Last week, corn rallied to 4-1/2 month highs as funds bought over 250 million bushels.

The market was expecting a cut in South Africa's maize output for 1997. Early Monday the Johannesburg-based National Maize Producers Organisation (Nampo) said hot and dry weather is likely to reduce this year's South African maize crop to between seven and 7.8 million tonnes. USDA in its February 12 supply/demand report pegged the crop at 9.5 million tonnes but is expected to revise that figure downward sometime this year.
Technicians early Monday cited first support in the March at $2.87-1/2 and second support at $2.81. The session low for March was $2.90-3/4.
First resistance was at $2.94 and second resistance was at $3.00-1/2. The session high for March was $2.92-1/4.
The four and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish flags early Monday.

But the short term nine day relative strength index (RSI) showed the market overbought and the March reached 84 percent at midsession. The market views an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.

Tenco Inc bought four million bushels of July and bought 2.5 million May, traders said. O'Connor and Co sold three million bushels of May, Dean Witter, Rosenthal Collins and Paine Webber each sold one million bushels of May, they said.
Large volume spread trades were noted with Smith Barney doing 12 million July/March and Continental Grain did eight million bushels of of March/July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 55,000 contracts, sharply below the 108,436 traded Friday.

In corn options, Refco Inc bought 800 May $2.90 calls and sold 800 May $3.10 calls, ING Derivatives bought 400 July $3.00 calls at 13-3/4 to 14 cents and Cargill Investor Services sold 500 July $3.00 calls at 13-3/4 to 14 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 34,000 contracts, below the 40,554 traded Friday.
